WG feat 38757 (and legacy 28411): three level-gated conditionals, all targeting PERCEPTION.
  conditional IF LEVEL LESS_THAN 12 -> addBonusToValue variable=PERCEPTION value=2 type=status text="to Seek and for initiative"
  conditional IF LEVEL >= 12 AND LEVEL < 20 -> addBonusToValue variable=PERCEPTION value=3 type=status
  conditional IF LEVEL EQUALS 20 -> addBonusToValue variable=PERCEPTION value=4 type=status
The legacy row 28411 additionally carries a bare `addBonusToValue` with NO variable and NO value (the op the parser calls unmapped) — it is an empty stub and the current row 38757 does not have it, so it carries no mechanical content.
investigation.oursDelivers: One situational (display-only) star, but aimed at the wrong stat: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:423 — "mediums-awareness": [{ targets: [{ kind: 'initiative' }], when: "to Seek and for initiative rolls", bonus: "+2 status (+3 at 12th, +4 at 20th)" }]. The bonus VALUES and the level escalation are right; the TARGET is not. No other carrier holds it: public/core.json feats.mediums-awareness has only actionCost/traits/aonId (no situational, recordMarks, passiveEffects), no RECORD_MARKERS entry, and no row in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json.
investigation.evidence: targetMatches (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:3264, case 'initiative' ~3288) returns true ONLY for ref.kind==='initiative' — its own comment says "An initiative bonus ... matches ONLY the initiative ref — never Perception." So explain.ts:1047 case 'perception' -> situationalList(..., featSituationalLines(c,db,ref)) (explain.ts:728) yields nothing for this feat, and hasFeatSituational (situationalBonuses.ts:4028) gives the Perception row no star. Result: the printed/WG half "+2 status bonus to Perception checks made to Seek" is delivered nowhere — a player reading Perception sees no note. AoN feat-7133 agrees with WG verbatim: "+2 status bonus to Perception checks made to Seek and when using Perception for your initiative roll." Only the initiative half reaches the sheet (explain.ts:1033).
investigation.fixSpec: Edit src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts line 423: change `targets: [{ kind: 'initiative' }]` to `targets: [{ kind: 'perception' }]`. Leave `when` and `bonus` strings untouched. Do NOT add both kinds — explain.ts:1037-1046 builds the Initiative popup by delegating to the Perception explain (`inner`) and then CONCATENATING its own initiative-targeted lines, so an entry carrying both targets would print twice in the Initiative popup. A perception-only target reaches both rows: it stars Perception (covering Seek) via explain.ts:1069 and rides into Initiative through the delegation at explain.ts:1037. This is exactly the shape situationalBonuses.ts:3285-3291 documents ("A Perception-SPECIFIC one ... stays targeted at `perception` and reaches the Initiative row through that breakdown's delegation instead, so neither kind is lost and neither double-counts") and the shape already used by the identical record "whispering-veil" at situationalBonuses.ts:1015 ("on Perception checks for initiative, and to Seek, Search…" -> [{ kind: 'perception' }]). No core.json or effect-backfill change needed.

investigation.theirEncoding:
WG feat 31308 (and legacy 29495) raw tree:
  select  optionType=ABILITY_BLOCK   ("Select a Feat")
  conditional
    IF FEAT_NAMES INCLUDES "barbarian resiliency"
    THEN
      addBonusToValue  variable=MAX_HEALTH_BONUS  value=+3
WG has no cross-record aggregation, so it pushes Barbarian Resiliency's per-archetype-feat HP onto EACH barbarian archetype feat, gated on owning Resiliency. The comparer keys by record id, so it sees an HP op on advanced-fury that our advanced-fury record does not have.
investigation.oursDelivers: Both halves, from the other end of the same relationship. (1) The select: src/rules/featPickGrants.ts:254 — 'advanced-fury': { prompt: "Choose a class feat", category: 'class', maxLevel: 'half', traits: ['barbarian'] } (the maxLevel:'half' encodes print's "barbarian level is equal to half your character level", which WG's bare ABILITY_BLOCK select does not). (2) The +3 HP: public/core.json feats['barbarian-resiliency'].maxHpBonus = {"perArchetypeFeat":3,"archetype":"barbarian"}, and public/core.json feats['advanced-fury'].archetype === "barbarian", so taking Advanced Fury raises the count by one and the total by exactly 3 — the same delta WG writes.
investigation.evidence: Reader chain for the select: build.ts:4185 `const spec = FEAT_PICK_GRANTS[fc.featId]` appends the picked feat to the built character (grantedBy handling at build.ts:7736-7745); the picker UI renders at Builder.tsx:2144-2146 and shared.tsx:2766. Reader chain for the HP: derive.ts:824-841 featHpBonus — `if (b.perArchetypeFeat && b.archetype) total += b.perArchetypeFeat * takenFeats.filter(x => x.archetype === b.archetype).length` — consumed by deriveMaxHp (derive.ts:843-854); the same fold runs at character-build time in build.ts:6976-6988 so starting HP matches. Barbarian archetype feats in core.json with archetype==='barbarian': barbarian-dedication, barbarian-resiliency, basic-fury, advanced-fury, instinct-ability, juggernauts-fortitude — advanced-fury is counted. Print (AoN feat-6193) says nothing about HP, so the whole HP op is the Resiliency interaction, which we own on the Resiliency record. Nothing to fix; the two encodings differ only in which record carries the row.

residualFindings.claim: The legendary-Intimidation reaction Demoralize is delivered by nothing.
residualFindings.printQuote: If you're legendary in Intimidation, you can use a reaction to Demoralize your foe when you critically succeed at an attack roll.
residualFindings.oursState: No carrier. This is Principle E territory (a reaction must appear with its trigger), but the feat's own actionCost is 'passive' and there is no action record to hang grantsActions on, so nothing surfaces it. Note extraReaction (types.ts:305) is NOT the lane — that field grants an ADDITIONAL restricted reaction per round, whereas this clause is a new use of your one reaction.
residualFindings.proposedFix: Same overlay row as above, as a second entry in the value array: {"on":"action","id":"demoralize","note":"If you're legendary in Intimidation you can Demoralize as a reaction when you critically succeed at an attack roll."} — rendered by the same chain (recordMarksFor explain.ts:392 -> recordMarkersFor explain.ts:594 -> MainTab.tsx:631). The proficiency gate is stated in the note, matching how RECORD_MARKERS entries such as titan-wrestler state their legendary clause in prose.

parityRead.evidence: THEIR op (row 20627): injectText {type:'action', id:19624 = «Demoralize» action, text = the feat's entire printed sentence}. OURS delivers NOTHING. core.json feats.terrified-retreat holds only {actionCost:{type:'passive'}} plus identity fields. A repo-wide grep for 'terrified-retreat' across src/ and scripts/data/ returns ZERO hits — no FEAT_SITUATIONAL key, no RECORD_MARKERS key, no effect-backfill/toggle-modes/consumable-modes row, no featGrants/featFeatGrants/featPickGrants/counterMods entry. It is also not in the degreeShifts lane: the only records with a demoralize degreeShift are flash-your-badge and talent-envy. So there is no live reader anywhere that renders this feat's content; the description prose is the entire surface.

residualFindings.claim: The item's activation frequency is stored as once per MINUTE, ten times more often than printed.
residualFindings.printQuote: **Activate** ⟨1⟩ Interact **Frequency** once per 10 minutes
residualFindings.oursState: core.json items.maestros-chair.frequency = {max:1, per:'minute'} and counters = [{id:'freq', label:'per minute', max:1, per:'minute', resetsOnRest:true}]. itemUses.ts:26-31 takes the explicit counters array in preference to the synthesized one, so InventoryTab.tsx:193 and ItemDetail.tsx:194 print the pip as 'per minute' while core-descriptions.json for the same item says 'once per 10 minutes' — the card contradicts itself and the player gets 10x the uses. The vocabulary for this exists (LimitedUses.every, types.ts:2112-2118, documented with 'once per 10 minutes' as its example) and 8 feat/classFeature records already use {max:1, per:'minute', every:10}.
residualFindings.proposedFix: Two overlay rows in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json (items.counters and items.frequency are both accepted fields): {"category":"items","id":"maestros-chair","field":"counters","value":[{"id":"freq","label":"per 10 minutes","max":1,"per":"minute","resetsOnRest":true}]} — the label is free text and is what itemUses.ts:58 hands to InventoryTab.tsx:193 / ItemDetail.tsx:194 — and {"category":"items","id":"maestros-chair","field":"frequency","value":{"max":1,"per":"minute","every":10}} so the synthesized fallback and any future reader of frequency.every agree.

residualFindings.claim: The Performance bonus is applied unconditionally although print restricts it to checks made with the chair, contrary to Ruling B.
residualFindings.printQuote: When you make a Performance check using your chair, you gain a +1 item bonus to the check.
residualFindings.oursState: The bonus lives in BOTH lanes: passiveEffects.skills.performance = 1 (effect-backfill.json:3914) adds +1 to every Performance check while the chair is in use (derive.ts:262 passiveItemBonus), and situationalBonuses.ts:1332 also states the restriction as a star. Ruling B ('a flat bonus the text restricts moves here, and leaves passiveEffects, so the total is right') was applied to the comparable instruments — arachnolute, benthic-drums, conch-of-otherworldly-seas, conductors-instrument, core-bugle, blakenshipper and booming-bell all have a 'while playing music with the instrument' star and passiveEffects = null. maestros-chair and bagpipes-of-turmoil are the two that kept the flat number, so a wheelchair user gets +1 to singing, oratory and dance too. NOTE FOR THE OWNER: WG also applies it flat (their addBonusToValue carries only a text scope), so this is print+Ruling B versus WG, not a WG gap.
residualFindings.proposedFix: Change the existing overlay row scripts/data/effect-backfill.json:3910-3918 {category:'items', id:'maestros-chair', field:'passiveEffects'} to "value": null (the null-deletes-the-field shape already used, e.g. the universal-versatility focusPoolBonus row at the head of the file), leaving situationalBonuses.ts:1332 as the whole delivery — exactly the shape the seven instrument items above ship. If the owner prefers WG's flat application instead, leave it and record the divergence; do not change it silently.
